nodes.label: Build Multi-Arch Image Workflow (build-image.yml)
nodes.rationale: Switched the explicit build target from the former python-based Dockerfile stages to node-runtime after Issue #250 introduced the TS toolchain and Issue #255 removed the Python builder/runtime stages entirely; node-runtime is now both the default final stage and the pushed production image.

nodes.label: Container Security Scan Workflow (Trivy)
nodes.rationale: Pins aquasecurity/trivy-action to an immutable commit SHA (v0.36.0 equivalent) instead of a mutable version tag, because a 2026-03-19 supply-chain attack (CVE-2026-33634 / GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23) rewrote most trivy-action version tags; GitHub's immutable-releases protection (>=v0.35.0) reduces but does not eliminate tag-rewrite risk, so SHA pinning is used for full safety.

nodes.label: Pre-commit Hooks Configuration
nodes.rationale: pre-commit remains the repository's permanent git hook entry point even after Issue #255 removed the Python toolchain (and the pyproject.toml-provided pre-commit dependency). Migrating the entry point to husky was considered and rejected: core.hooksPath is written to .git/config, which is shared across all git worktrees of the repo, so pointing it at husky would disable pre-commit-enforced checks (betterleaks secret scanning, pymarkdown, etc.) in every other concurrently checked-out worktree. This constraint holds regardless of language, so it is not superseded by the Python removal.

nodes.label: code-review-agent Pod Manifest
nodes.rationale: Uses exec probes (python -c urllib.request...) instead of httpGet probes: podman kube play translates httpGet into 'curl -f URL', but the hardened runtime image contains neither a shell nor curl, whereas an exec probe bypasses CMD-SHELL and runs Python directly, which does exist in the image.

nodes.label: ADR-0001: Large-Diff Review Scope Policy
nodes.rationale: Adopts staged defense-in-depth: implement Option 1 (graduated per-file/per-PR character-limit trimming, replacing the existing all-or-nothing patch=None binary fallback) first, then Option 2 (explicit per-file exclusion flag propagated through FileChange→ReviewResult→LeadEngineerReport) second; Option 3 (whole-PR exclusion) is deferred as a future circuit breaker. Rationale: the binary fallback caused a documented failure (hoppscotch/hoppscotch#6171) where all patches were dropped to None, triggering an MCP fetch storm, turn-budget exhaustion, and a StructuredOutputMissingError absent from INFRA_EXCEPTIONS — producing a silently empty ReviewReport indistinguishable from 'PR has no issues'. Graduated trimming preserves degraded patch content so reviewers rely less on sequential per-file MCP fetches; per-file exclusion further prevents a single oversized file from re-triggering the same failure while making the omission explicit rather than silent.

nodes.label: ADR-0002: Workflow Externalization (LangFlow/Dify)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the structured (schema-validated) output contract and defers the decision on delegating flow control to LangFlow/Dify. Message-based (free-text) output would remove the StructuredOutputMissingError failure mode but only relocates the parsing burden to a downstream node/evaluation script rather than eliminating it, and would break the evaluation pipeline's direct JSONL parsing; the existing AgentCard.outputSchema design was already chosen specifically so an A2A client (including LangFlow/Dify) can validate the JSON Schema directly, so staying structured is consistent with that prior decision.

nodes.label: ADR-0003: GitHub MCP Startup Retry Strategy
nodes.rationale: Retries only MCPClient.start() (not individual tool calls or full reviewer/collector re-execution), using exponential backoff with jitter (tenacity, stop_after_attempt(3), ~1s base wait), because Issue #115's root cause is simultaneous-connection congestion: immediate or fixed-interval retries reproduce the same congestion, and backoff without jitter still synchronizes retry timing across the up-to-6 concurrent sessions that fail together — jitter is the only strategy that actively de-synchronizes the retries. Also adds ToolProviderException to INFRA_EXCEPTIONS so exhausted retries on the reviewer path are re-raised as infra failures instead of being silently downgraded to a business-logic ReviewError.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003: github mcp startup retry strategy

nodes.label: ADR-0004: MCP Client Session Sharing (Between Reviewers)
nodes.rationale: Shares one MCP connection only across the concurrently-running reviewer set (not across PR-info-collection, and not process-wide), using the strands MCPClient's built-in reference-counting consumer model (add_consumer/remove_consumer) rather than a hand-rolled manager or connection pool. Tracing the actual pipeline showed PR-info-collection and parallel review never overlap in time, so only reviewer-to-reviewer concurrency (currently 2 sessions) is the real congestion; a pool would be over-engineering for 2 concurrent consumers, and reference counting reuses a mechanism the framework already provides instead of building new state management.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0004: mcp client session sharing (between reviewers)

nodes.label: ADR-0005: Stack-Specific Gold-Set Target Selection Canonicalization
nodes.rationale: Fully retires the old single-pool tagged-target route (convert_tagged_targets.py / pr_targets_b2b2c_tagged.json) in favor of the new per-stack producer (discover_candidate_prs.py → pr_targets_{stack}.json) as the sole canonical evaluation-target input, and consolidates the production-code and inline-comment eligibility predicates that the producer and build_gold_set.py had been applying inconsistently into a single shared predicate module both import. PR #145 introduced the per-stack producer but nothing consumed it, so severity/impact/priority scoring sat unused; keeping both paths (rejected) would leave the 'which path is canonical' ambiguity unresolved and duplicate incompatible schemas, and loosening the Gold builder to match the producer's laxer criteria (also rejected) would violate EVALUATION_PLAN.md §2.0.2's inline-comment requirement.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005: stack-specific gold-set target selection canonicalization

nodes.label: Issue #255: Python→TypeScript Migration Completed
nodes.rationale: Completed the Python→TypeScript migration: removed the former src/code_review_agent/ tree, removed the Dockerfile's python-builder/python-runtime stages (node-runtime is now the only/default final stage), and removed Python-only pre-commit hooks (ruff/pyright) plus the pyproject.toml-based pre-commit install path, without promoting husky as a replacement hook entry point.

nodes.label: A2A TaskStore Design (per-module in-memory Map, owner check, 30-min TTL)
nodes.rationale: Each module owns an independent in-memory Map-based TaskStore (no external store like Redis) because the process is a single-process monolith; get(taskId, ownerPrincipalId) returns null on owner mismatch so callers can treat it uniformly as 404; a 30-minute unref()'d deletion timer is scheduled on completion/failure/creation so results don't accumulate in memory indefinitely, chosen over adding an external KV store dependency.
nodes.norm_label: a2a taskstore design (per-module in-memory map, owner check, 30-min ttl)

nodes.label: A2A API Authentication: GitHub OAuth Bearer Token
nodes.rationale: Chose validating Authorization: Bearer <github_access_token> against GET https://api.github.com/user over an X-API-Key scheme (rejected: independent key rotation/revocation cost), a third-party IdP like Entra ID/Auth0 (rejected: unnecessary extra IdP dependency since users are already GitHub users), or no auth (rejected: a network misconfiguration would fully expose task submission). GitHub OAuth simultaneously solves authentication and github_token acquisition for downstream calls.
nodes.norm_label: a2a api authentication: github oauth bearer token

nodes.label: A2A API SSRF Mitigation: Server-Env-Only llm_base_url
nodes.rationale: CODE_REVIEW_LLM_BASE_URL is configured only via server environment variables and never accepted in the request body, to prevent a client from directing the server to fetch an internal/cloud-metadata address (e.g. AWS IMDSv1 169.254.169.254) as an SSRF vector; URL allowlisting/validation was rejected as insufficient because DNS rebinding and similar techniques can bypass it.
nodes.norm_label: a2a api ssrf mitigation: server-env-only llm_base_url

nodes.label: A2A API Error Sanitization (sanitizeError, token redaction)
nodes.rationale: sanitizeError() replaces Bearer <token>, ghp_*, gho_*, github_pat_* patterns with [REDACTED] before persisting a failed task's error message, to prevent GitHub token leakage when the GitHub MCP client's exception text happens to embed the Authorization header value; every module's service.ts duplicates this function rather than centralizing it, deliberately mirroring the modules' otherwise-independent per-module TaskStore design.
nodes.norm_label: a2a api error sanitization (sanitizeerror, token redaction)

nodes.label: Unmounted /health Module Gap (Issue #362)
nodes.rationale: The health module (modules/health/) is fully implemented at the service/route layer but its mount into index.ts was deliberately deferred to a separate slice during the TS/Zod migration; meanwhile index.ts hardcodes port 3000 while the evaluation pipeline's container-startup script polls http://localhost:8000/health, and how (or whether) that health check currently succeeds is unconfirmed without actually starting the container.

nodes.label: Issue #54: Patch Size Overload Mitigation
nodes.rationale: Proposed staged/graduated trimming (5,000 chars/file, 40,000 chars/PR) to address model context overload and 1800s timeouts on huge PRs (e.g. mui/material-ui#48325, 46 files/~148K chars); the implementation that actually shipped was a binary (all-or-nothing) fallback rather than the proposed graduated trimming — same issue name, different actual mechanism.

nodes.label: Binary Patch Fallback Failure Mode (findings=0 ambiguity)
nodes.rationale: 5-whys causal chain: an oversized PR (e.g. hoppscotch/hoppscotch#6171, 23 files/35,106 chars) exceeds patch_total_char_limit=30,000 → all target_files' patch fields are set to None → reviewer falls back to sequential per-file GitHub MCP get_file_contents calls → a tool-name resolution error adds wasted retries → granite4.1:8b fails to converge on the ReviewOutput schema within max_agent_turns=30 → StructuredOutputMissingError is raised, absent from INFRA_EXCEPTIONS, so review_orchestrator.py records it as a business error rather than re-raising it → ReviewReport.results ends up empty → agent_predictions.jsonl records findings=0, indistinguishable from a genuinely clean PR.
nodes.norm_label: binary patch fallback failure mode (findings=0 ambiguity)

nodes.label: Issue #115: GitHub MCP Connection Instability
nodes.rationale: 10 of 18 Seeded-set PRs failed evaluation due to GitHub MCP connection errors (background thread did not start in 30 seconds / Connection to the MCP server was closed / empty-body JSON parse failures); root cause is simultaneous-session congestion — ReviewOrchestrator.run_async fans out registered reviewers via asyncio.to_thread, so up to 3 MCP sessions per PR combine with --concurrency 2 to produce up to 6 concurrent handshake attempts against MCPClient's default 30s startup_timeout, with no retry/backoff. Root-caused two remediation directions: (1) startup retry (ADR-0003) and (2) session sharing (ADR-0004).

nodes.label: Angular CLI
nodes.rationale: Always prefer `ng add`/`ng generate` over manual npm install or hand-written files because CLI schematics also run initialization/config steps (angular.json updates, provider registration), which manual edits would miss.

nodes.label: Component Test Harness
nodes.rationale: Harnesses are preferred over direct DOM queries because they decouple tests from internal DOM structure, so refactors that change markup do not break tests; the same harness is reusable across unit and e2e tests.

nodes.label: Component Styling / View Encapsulation
nodes.rationale: Emulated encapsulation (default) balances style scoping with backwards compatibility (global leaks still possible); ShadowDom gives full isolation via native browser API; None makes styles global; ::ng-deep is discouraged by the Angular team and kept only for backwards compatibility.

nodes.label: Template Control Flow (@if/@for/@switch)
nodes.rationale: `@for` requires a `track` expression for performance/DOM reuse; `@switch` uses strict equality with no fallthrough, and `@default never;` gives exhaustive type checking for unions.

nodes.label: Service (@Service decorator)
nodes.rationale: @Service is the recommended default because it creates a singleton, makes it available application-wide without a providers array, and enables tree-shaking; autoProvided:false is used only when a component needs its own isolated instance.

nodes.label: Route Data Resolver (ResolveFn)
nodes.rationale: Resolvers should stay lightweight because navigation is blocked and the UI stays on the old page until the resolver finishes; global loading feedback via router events is recommended to offset this.

nodes.label: Route Definition (Routes array)
nodes.rationale: Angular uses first-match-wins matching, so specific routes must be ordered before less specific ones and the wildcard `**` route must be placed last.

nodes.label: Dependency Provider (providers array / InjectionToken)
nodes.rationale: Manual providers (useClass/useValue/useFactory/useExisting/multi) are needed when a service lacks providedIn, when a fresh instance per component is required, or when configuring runtime values; library authors should expose provide* functions to encapsulate configuration instead of raw provider objects.

nodes.label: Dependency Injection (DI) Fundamentals
nodes.rationale: DI improves maintainability, scalability, and testability by separating providing (making values available) from injecting (requesting them) so components/services don't construct their own dependencies.

nodes.label: End-to-End (E2E) Testing Setup
nodes.rationale: Setup guidance should only be applied if no E2E framework is already configured, or if the user explicitly requests changing/setting one up, to avoid clobbering an existing test setup.

nodes.label: Effect / afterRenderEffect
nodes.rationale: Effects must never be used to propagate/sync signal state (calling .set()/.update() inside an effect) because it causes ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenChecked errors and infinite loops; computed()/linkedSignal() should be used for state derivation instead. afterRenderEffect enforces read/write phase separation (earlyRead -> write -> mixedReadWrite -> read) to prevent layout thrashing, and only runs client-side, never during SSR.

nodes.label: Environment Configuration (build-time vs runtime)
nodes.rationale: Build-time environment files are bundled client-side and must never hold secrets/API keys; choose build-time config for faster startup and lower complexity, and runtime config (loaded via provideAppInitializer) only when the same build artifact must be deployed across multiple environments without rebuilding.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Injectors (EnvironmentInjector / ElementInjector)
nodes.rationale: Resolution checks the ElementInjector tree first, then the EnvironmentInjector tree, before throwing; `providers` exposes a service to a component's view and projected content, while `viewProviders` withholds it from projected content to isolate services from consumers.

nodes.label: Component Host Element Binding
nodes.rationale: The `host` object in @Component is preferred over legacy @HostBinding/@HostListener decorators; on binding collisions, consumer static bindings beat component static bindings, dynamic bindings beat static ones, and the component's own host binding wins between two dynamic bindings.

nodes.label: Injection Context
nodes.rationale: inject() only works inside an injection context (field initializers, constructors, factory functions, or Angular-executed functional APIs); runInInjectionContext lets code run with a borrowed injector outside those spots, and assertInInjectionContext lets utility authors fail fast with a clear error instead of a confusing one.

nodes.label: Signal-based Component Input (input())
nodes.rationale: input()/input.required()/model() are preferred over the legacy @Input() decorator for better reactivity, type safety, and build-time errors on missing required inputs; transform functions must stay pure and statically analyzable.

nodes.label: linkedSignal
nodes.rationale: Use computed() when state is strictly derived and never manually overridden; use linkedSignal() when derived state must still be user-overridable while resetting when its source changes; never use effect() to sync one signal to another.

nodes.label: Route Loading Strategies (eager vs lazy)
nodes.rationale: Eager loading gives seamless transitions but grows the initial bundle; lazy loading (loadComponent/loadChildren) keeps the initial bundle small at the cost of an extra fetch on navigation. Recommendation: eager-load primary landing pages, lazy-load everything else.

nodes.label: Angular CLI MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Ships default read/analysis tools (list_projects, get_best_practices, onpush_zoneless_migration, search_documentation) while build/test/e2e/devserver tools are gated behind --experimental-tool so project-modifying or long-running actions require explicit opt-in.

nodes.label: Automatic Migrations & Code Modernization
nodes.rationale: Official schematics are preferred over manual text replacement for modernization; the standalone migration specifically must be run as three discrete, separately-verified phases (convert to standalone, remove NgModules, bootstrap via standalone APIs) because doing it in one pass risks an unbuildable intermediate state.

nodes.label: Signal-based Component Output (output())
nodes.rationale: output() is preferred over @Output()/EventEmitter; output names should use camelCase without an `on` prefix and must avoid colliding with native DOM event names since custom events do not bubble like native DOM events.
